reason: While the evidence supports that iGlarLixi (insulin glargine 100 units/mL + lixisenatide) is indicated for adults with type 2 diabetes insufficiently controlled on basal insulin or oral agents, the claim substantially broadens the label scope. Revise the indication statement to include the required restrictions: patients with obesity, use as an adjunct to diet and exercise in addition to metformin (with or without SGLT2 inhibitors), and failure specifically on metformin alone or metformin combined with specified oral agents or basal insulin.

panel_findings.statement: In the LixiLan-L pivotal trial data, the LS mean change in body weight from baseline for Insulin glargine 100 units/mL (n=365) was +0.7 ± 0.2 kg in patients insufficiently controlled on basal insulin (+ metformin ± 1-2 OADs).
In the LixiLan-L pivotal trial data, the LS mean change in body weight from baseline for SOLIQUA (n=366) was -0.7 ± 0.2 kg with p<0.0001 compared to insulin glargine.
In the SoliMix pivotal trial data after 26 weeks, the change in body weight for Premix Insulin BIAsp 30 (n=444) was +1.2 ± 0.2 kg in patients insufficiently controlled on basal insulin + OADs.
In the SoliMix pivotal trial data after 26 weeks, the change in body weight for SOLIQUA (n=443) was -0.7 ± 0.2 kg with p<0.0001 compared to Premix Insulin BIAsp 30.

In the propensity score matching analysis (LixiLan-L and GGD2), the mean change in weight from baseline for Basal bolus therapy (n=195) was +0.70 ± 0.24 kg in patients insufficiently controlled on basal insulins.
In the propensity score matching analysis (LixiLan-L and GGD2), the mean change in weight from baseline for SOLIQUA (n=195) was -0.62 ± 0.24 kg with p<0.0001 compared to Basal bolus therapy.
